content: The world is all the richer for having a devil in it, so long as we keep our foot upon his neck.
author: William James
sourceWork: Pragmatism: A New Name for Some Old Ways of Thinking (1907)
story:
Rather than offering a polite platitude, this observation challenges how we navigate our inner lives. We spend enormous energy trying to present a sanitized, perfect version of ourselves to the world. But whatever emotions or desires we push into the dark don't disappear; they run our lives from behind the curtain.

Across his life and work, William James saw how easily we surrender our tranquility to fear, vanity, and distraction. True maturity isn't pretending you have no dark corners—it is having the honesty and courage to look at your jealousy, fear, and anger in the daylight so they no longer control your actions.
reflectionPrompt: How can acknowledging your vulnerability help you build deeper self-trust and inner peace?

practicalInsight: Notice what traits in other people irritate you most. Ask yourself honestly if you carry a dormant seed of that same trait within yourself.
